html:
Early Turkic tribes is the map's label for the steppe and forest peoples north of Mongolia around 200 BCE, thought to be ancestors of the Turkic-speaking peoples. Nobody can be sure what language anyone spoke then, since Turkic was first written only in the 700s, in the Orkhon inscriptions.

Chinese records name peoples in this area such as the Dingling and the Gekun, early forms of the Kyrgyz. Around 200 BCE Modu Chanyu made them subjects of the Xiongnu. Centuries later their heirs founded the Türk Khaganates and spread west in the Turkic migrations.
